And that's what Dream Makers do: low cost, big delight.
We hope agents‘ help can ensure the service baseline, while Dream Makers raise the service ceiling.

When we visited the Mandarin Oriental in Shenzhen, the lobby manager shared a lot of interesting story about how dream makers work. Spot a guest moment, arrange a surprise, and deliver it. But we saw three challenges: too much depends on individual judgment, ideas come from personal inspiration, and lessons from each surprise aren't captured.
So our question is: how might we help Dream Makers recognise emerging guest preferences and turn them into timely, feasible hotel responses?
Based on our three natural interactions, discover, arrange and execute. we redesigned the Dream Maker workflow.

First, instead of relying only on individual judgement, guest data helps identify delight opportunities.
Second, instead of relying only on personal creativity, AI and a shared database help find solutions.

Finally, instead of treating each surprise as a one-off experience, AI helps capture and structure successful cases for future reuse.

So, we're turning individual experience into shared intelligence.

Until finally, this solution delivers strong business value for MO.
First, retention increases 15 to 25 percent through easy booking and butler surprises.
Second, capture rate jumps to 97.5 percent with visual options.
Third, request entry time drops from 5 to 3 minutes.
Lastly, built for VIP agents, it scales to all guests—cutting offline complaints to zero.

Yet, realistically, we recognize three potential risks.
First, to control system costs, we deploy lightweight plug-in pages.
Second, to lower training costs, we offer an intuitive backend and Streamlined SOP.
Third, customized booking sets higher expectations—so we need real-time inventory and prototype testing to fully validate fulfillment.

In short, we believe optimizing just two touchpoints can offer a low-risk, scalable path to real growth.
